title: Count Number of Maximum Bitwise-OR Subsets
statement: A subset of the integer array `nums` is formed by choosing some positions of `nums` (at least one) and keeping the values there; subsets are told apart by the positions chosen, so equal values at different positions give different subsets. The OR of a subset is the bitwise OR of all its values. First find the largest OR any non-empty subset can reach, then return how many non-empty subsets have exactly that OR.
notes:
## Intuition

OR only ever adds bits, so the biggest OR is reached by the whole array: `target` is simply the OR of every value. With at most 16 values there are at most `2^16 = 65,536` subsets, so we can afford to visit them all. Backtracking does that by deciding, value by value, whether to take it or leave it, carrying the OR built so far down the recursion.

## Approach

1. OR every value together to get `target`.
2. `backtrack(index, current)` has already decided the values before `index`, and `current` is the OR of the ones taken.
3. When `index` reaches the end, one subset is complete: if `current === target`, add one to `count`.
4. Otherwise branch twice: take `nums[index]` (OR it into `current`) or skip it.
5. Start with `backtrack(0, 0)` and return `count`. The empty subset has OR `0`, which never equals `target` because every value is at least 1, so it is never counted.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 1]`, so `target = 3 | 1 = 3`. The four leaves are:

| take 3? | take 1? | current | counted? |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 3 | yes |
| yes | no | 3 | yes |
| no | yes | 1 | no |
| no | no | 0 | no |

`count = 2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(2^n): the recursion tree has `2^n` leaves and each step is O(1).
- Space: O(n) for the recursion depth.

## Pitfalls

- Count subsets by positions: `[2, 2, 2]` has 7 subsets with OR 2, not 1.
- Do not search for the maximum separately; the OR of the whole array is always the maximum.
- Exclude the empty subset; here it is excluded automatically because its OR is `0`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `target` | OR of all of `nums`, the largest possible subset OR |
| `count` | subsets found whose OR equals `target` |
| `index` | the next position to decide on |
| `current` | OR of the values taken so far |

narration.4: OR can only add bits, so the OR of the whole array is the largest possible subset OR.
narration.6: No matching subset has been found yet.
narration.8: Decide value by value; current is the OR of the values taken so far.

narration.10: Does this subset reach the maximum OR?
narration.15: Branch 1: take nums[index] and add its bits.
narration.16: Branch 2: skip nums[index] and keep the OR unchanged.

narration.20: Return the number of subsets whose OR is the maximum.
